signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 191.841, reflecting an exceptional 1.505% leader-to-laggard weekly performance gap across G10 peers. CHF leads the G10 basket up +0.761% over 6 pairs, underpinned by a dominant Economic Surprise Index reading of +22.1. Conversely, JPY anchors the performance table down −0.744% across 7 pairs despite an accommodative real policy rate of −1.45% and negative 2Y yield momentum of −10bp over 5 sessions. The bilateral divergence occurs despite a 125bp nominal policy rate deficit favoring JPY, demonstrating that sovereign macro momentum and relative macro data beats are overriding negative nominal carry. The pair holds firmly in an established uptrend ahead of this morning's Swiss National Bank policy assessment. Trade bias: Long CHF/JPY; robust economic surprises override the nominal carry penalty. Catalyst: SNB Interest Rate Decision today at 07:30 UTC. Risk: SNB delivers an unexpected dovish pushback on exchange rate strength, compressing the 1.505% bilateral spread.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Options Downside Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY prints at 157.668, holding above its SMA20 of 156.61 while remaining capped beneath the 50-day and 200-day moving averages at 158.85 and 158.42. The fundamental bid remains supported by a substantial 287bp SOFR vs TONA overnight index swap carry advantage alongside an explicit 275bp Fed-BoJ policy rate differential. However, options dynamics reflect stark asymmetry, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal displaying an extreme put skew of −2.27. Additionally, 1M implied volatility sits at 7.9% against a 30-day realized volatility of 9.7%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of −1.8% that signals complacency in spot pricing relative to tail protection demand. The divergence indicates that institutional desks are paying a premium for downside insurance while spot is carried higher by the yield buffer. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY; underlying rate carry maintains spot demand against institutional options hedging. Catalyst: BoJ Trimmed Mean Core CPI. Risk: Spot falls below the SMA20 anchor at 156.61, triggering downside options gamma and accelerating an unwind toward 155.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning Extends
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.70990, testing immediate chart support directly between its rising SMA50 at 0.7094 and descending SMA20 at 0.7164. CFTC positioning highlights an increasingly crowded institutional long, with leveraged funds holding net longs of +59,299 contracts, marking the 97th percentile of its trailing 52-week distribution with a z-score of +2.11. Despite levered accounts adding +10,920 contracts WoW, spot has failed to clear the 0.7164 moving average ceiling, illustrating stalling upside momentum amidst elevated positioning. While a 50bp AONIA over SOFR overnight cash spread provides underlying carry support, this heavy institutional positioning leaves the currency vulnerable to swift liquidations on any broader risk deterioration. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish AUD/USD; positioning saturation limits further upside follow-through. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change on 24 Sep. Risk: Daily close below the SMA50 support at 0.7094 confirms technical exhaustion and triggers speculative unwinds.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Macro Divergence + Technical Resistance Cluster
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.14270, remaining entrenched beneath its complete daily moving-average stack including the SMA20 at 1.1576, SMA50 at 1.1542, and SMA200 at 1.1629. Cross central bank fundamentals continue to favor the greenback, with Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% delivering a 135bp nominal policy differential and a 141bp OIS carry premium supporting USD. Sovereign bond spreads reflect persistent US yield leadership, with the German-US 2Y yield differential widening 15bp in USD's favor over the trailing 5 sessions to −158bp. Leveraged funds hold net short exposure of −51,355 contracts at the 32nd percentile of the 52-week range, confirming specs are aligned with the prevailing policy rate gap. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; macro carry spreads and moving-average structure reinforce downside drift. Catalyst: Euro Area Flash PMIs today at 08:00 UTC. Risk: Flash composite PMI prints substantially above the 51.1 consensus, lifting European short-end yields and sparking a technical squeeze toward 1.1542.
